page.title: Lisp and Scheme
page.desc: John McCarthy's Lisp (1958) introduced symbolic expressions, code as data, and garbage collection; Scheme (1975) distilled it with lexical scope and tail calls, and Clojure (2007) brought it to the JVM.
page.intro: John McCarthy's Lisp (1958) introduced symbolic expressions, code as data, and garbage collection; Scheme (1975) distilled it with lexical scope and tail calls, and Clojure (2007) brought it to the JVM.

synapses.text: Programs are lists, so macros can transform code before it runs; this homoiconicity is Lisp's defining feature.

synapses.lead: Garbage collection was invented for Lisp
synapses.text: McCarthy described automatic reclamation of list cells in 1959.
Proper tail-call optimisation is required by the Scheme standard, so loops are written as recursion.
